items.title: mlx-cluster
items.text:
mlx-cluster provides fast graph algorithms for Apple's MLX framework: random walks, neighbor sampling, and sparse x dense matrix multiplication (SpMM) for GNN message passing. It is a C++ extension of MLX with Metal kernels, and the sampling and sparse backend of mlx-graphs.

pip install mlx-cluster

items.title: What's inside
items.text:
• Random walks: uniform walks (random_walk) and Node2Vec biased walks with p / q (rejection_sampling), on CPU and GPU.
  • Neighbor sampling: multi-hop GraphSAGE sampling (neighbor_sample), heterogeneous graphs (hetero_neighbor_sample) and meta-path walks (metapath_random_walk).
  • Fused message passing: SpMM with sum, mean, max and min, with gradients, in COO (spmm_coo) and load-balanced CSR (spmm_csr) formats.
  • Attention scores: multi-head dot products per edge (edge_scores) without per-edge feature arrays.

items.title: Where to go next
items.text:

items.title: rejection_sampling
items.text:
rejection_sampling(
    rowptr: mlx.core.array,
    col: mlx.core.array,
    start: mlx.core.array,
    walk_length: int,
    p: float,
    q: float,
    *,
    key: object | None = None,
    max_attempts: int = 1000,
    stream: object | None = None,
) -> tuple

node2vec biased random walks (rejection sampling).

Having moved t -> v, the next node x is a neighbor of v chosen with weight 1/p if x == t, 1 if x is a neighbor of t, and 1/q otherwise. A node without neighbors keeps the walk in place (edge id -1).

Random numbers are generated inside the kernel from a counter-based generator seeded by key, so the CPU and GPU produce identical walks for the same key.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rowptr array

CSR row pointers (int64).

required col array

CSR column indices (int64).

required start array

Start nodes (int64).

required walk_length int

Number of steps per walk.

required p float

Return parameter; larger values make returning to the previous node less likely.

required q float

In-out parameter; q > 1 keeps walks local (BFS-like), q < 1 pushes them outward (DFS-like).

required key array

uint32 key with 2 elements, e.g. mx.random.key(0). If omitted, one is drawn from MLX's global RNG, so mx.random.seed makes walks reproducible.

None max_attempts int

Rejection-sampling cap per step. After this many rejections the last candidate is accepted. Default 1000.

1000 stream Stream | Device

Where to run (mx.cpu or mx.gpu).

None

Returns:

Type Description tuple (mlx.core.array, mlx.core.array

(nodes, edges) of

tuple

shapes [len(start), walk_length + 1] and

[len(start), walk_length], both int64.

def hetero_neighbor_sample(
    colptr_dict: Mapping[EdgeType, mx.array],
    row_dict: Mapping[EdgeType, mx.array],
    seed_dict: Mapping[NodeType, mx.array],
    num_neighbors: NumNeighbors,
    num_nodes_dict: Optional[Mapping[NodeType, int]] = None,
    replace: bool = False,
    directed: bool = True,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
) -> HeteroSamplerOutput:
    """Multi-hop neighbor sampling on a heterogeneous graph (GraphSAGE style).

    For every edge type ``(src, rel, dst)`` and every hop, up to ``k``
    incoming ``src`` neighbors are sampled for each ``dst`` node discovered
    at the previous hop (the seeds at hop 0).

    Args:
        colptr_dict: CSC column pointers per edge type. For ``(src, rel,
            dst)`` this has ``num_dst_nodes + 1`` int64 entries.
        row_dict: CSC row indices (source node of each edge, sorted by
            destination) per edge type, int64.
        seed_dict: Seed node ids per node type. Must not contain duplicates.
        num_neighbors: Fan-out per hop, e.g. ``[10, 5]``. Either a single
            list used for every edge type, or a dict mapping each edge type
            to its own list. ``-1`` takes all neighbors; ``0`` samples none.
            Shorter lists are padded with ``0``.
        num_nodes_dict: Optional number of nodes per node type (e.g.
            ``HeteroGraphData.num_nodes``). Lets node types that only appear
            as a source use the faster dense id mapper.
        replace: Sample with replacement.
        directed: Only ``True`` is supported for heterogeneous graphs.
        seed: Seed for the sampler's RNG. If ``None``, one is drawn from
            MLX's global RNG, so ``mx.random.seed(...)`` makes sampling
            reproducible.

    Returns:
        HeteroSamplerOutput

    Example:

    .. code-block:: python

        out = hetero_neighbor_sample(
            colptr_dict={("author", "writes", "paper"): colptr},
            row_dict={("author", "writes", "paper"): row},
            seed_dict={"paper": mx.array([0, 1], dtype=mx.int64)},
            num_neighbors=[10, 5],
        )
        out.node_id["author"]                         # sampled author ids
        et = ("author", "writes", "paper")
        edge_index = mx.stack([out.row[et], out.col[et]])
    """
    edge_types = list(colptr_dict.keys())
    if not edge_types:
        raise ValueError("colptr_dict must contain at least one edge type")
    if set(row_dict.keys()) != set(edge_types):
        raise ValueError("colptr_dict and row_dict must have the same edge types")
    if not seed_dict:
        raise ValueError("seed_dict must contain at least one node type")

    rel_types = [edge_type_to_str(et) for et in edge_types]

    # Node types: everything mentioned by edge types, seeds or num_nodes_dict,
    # in first-seen order (deterministic output ordering).
    node_types: List[str] = []
    for et in edge_types:
        for nt in (et[0], et[2]):
            if nt not in node_types:
                node_types.append(nt)
    for nt in list(seed_dict.keys()) + list((num_nodes_dict or {}).keys()):
        if nt not in node_types:
            node_types.append(nt)

    fanouts = _resolve_num_neighbors(num_neighbors, edge_types)

    seeds = {}
    for nt, s in seed_dict.items():
        s = s if isinstance(s, mx.array) else mx.array(s)
        seeds[nt] = s.astype(mx.int64).reshape(-1)

    if seed is None:
        seed = int(mx.random.randint(0, 2**31 - 1, shape=()).item())

    node_id, row, col, edge_id, n_nodes, n_edges = _hetero_neighbor_sample(
        node_types,
        edge_types,
        {rt: colptr_dict[et] for rt, et in zip(rel_types, edge_types)},
        {rt: row_dict[et] for rt, et in zip(rel_types, edge_types)},
        seeds,
        {rt: fanouts[et] for rt, et in zip(rel_types, edge_types)},
        {k: int(v) for k, v in (num_nodes_dict or {}).items()},
        bool(replace),
        bool(directed),
        int(seed),
    )

    to_et = dict(zip(rel_types, edge_types))
    return HeteroSamplerOutput(
        node_id={nt: node_id[nt] for nt in node_types},
        row={to_et[rt]: row[rt] for rt in rel_types},
        col={to_et[rt]: col[rt] for rt in rel_types},
        edge_id={to_et[rt]: edge_id[rt] for rt in rel_types},
        num_sampled_nodes={nt: list(n_nodes[nt]) for nt in node_types},
        num_sampled_edges={to_et[rt]: list(n_edges[rt]) for rt in rel_types},
    )

def build_metapath_csr(
    edge_index_dict: Mapping[EdgeType, mx.array],
    metapath: Sequence[EdgeType],
    num_nodes_dict: Optional[Mapping[NodeType, int]] = None,
) -> MetaPathCSR:
    """Builds the CSR adjacency used by :func:`metapath_random_walk`.

    This sorts every relation once, so compute it once per graph and reuse it.

    Args:
        edge_index_dict: ``(src, rel, dst) -> [2, num_edges]`` edge indices,
            with node ids local to each node type (as in ``HeteroGraphData``).
        metapath: List of ``(src, rel, dst)`` edge types. Each edge type must
            end at the node type the next one starts from.
        num_nodes_dict: Optional number of nodes per node type. Missing types
            are inferred from the largest node id in ``edge_index_dict``.

    Returns:
        MetaPathCSR
    """
    metapath = _validate_metapath(metapath)
    missing = [et for et in metapath if et not in edge_index_dict]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Edge types {missing} are not in edge_index_dict")

    num_nodes = _infer_num_nodes(edge_index_dict, num_nodes_dict)

    unique_rels: List[EdgeType] = []
    for et in metapath:
        if et not in unique_rels:
            unique_rels.append(et)

    rowptrs, cols, rp_off, col_off = [], [], [], []
    rp_cursor, col_cursor = 0, 0
    for et in unique_rels:
        src_type = et[0]
        n_src = num_nodes.get(src_type, 0)
        ei = np.asarray(edge_index_dict[et]).astype(np.int64)
        src, dst = ei[0], ei[1]
        order = np.argsort(src, kind="stable")
        counts = np.bincount(src, minlength=n_src)
        rowptr = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(counts)]).astype(np.int64)
        rowptrs.append(rowptr)
        cols.append(dst[order])
        rp_off.append(rp_cursor)
        col_off.append(col_cursor)
        rp_cursor += rowptr.shape[0]
        col_cursor += dst.shape[0]

    return MetaPathCSR(
        metapath=metapath,
        rowptr=mx.array(np.concatenate(rowptrs)),
        col=mx.array(np.concatenate(cols)),
        rowptr_offset=mx.array(np.array(rp_off, dtype=np.int64)),
        col_offset=mx.array(np.array(col_off, dtype=np.int64)),
        rel_ids=[unique_rels.index(et) for et in metapath],
        num_nodes_dict=num_nodes,
    )

def metapath_random_walk(
    csr: MetaPathCSR,
    start: mx.array,
    walk_length: int,
    rand: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    stream: Optional[mx.Stream] = None,
) -> Tuple[mx.array, mx.array]:
    """Meta-path guided uniform random walks.

    Step ``l`` of every walk follows edge type ``metapath[l % len(metapath)]``,
    choosing uniformly among the current node's neighbors of that type. If a
    node has no such neighbor, the walk stops and the remaining entries are
    ``-1``.

    Args:
        csr: Output of :func:`build_metapath_csr`.
        start: Start node ids, local to ``metapath[0][0]``'s node type.
        walk_length: Number of steps per walk. If it is longer than the
            meta-path, the meta-path must be cyclic (end where it starts).
        rand: Optional uniform ``[0, 1)`` values of shape
            ``[len(start), walk_length]``. Drawn from MLX's RNG if omitted,
            so ``mx.random.seed`` makes walks reproducible.
        stream: Stream or device to run on (``mx.cpu`` or ``mx.gpu``).

    Returns:
        tuple ``(nodes, edges)``: ``nodes`` is ``[len(start), walk_length + 1]``
        local node ids (the type of column ``j`` is
        ``metapath_node_types(metapath, walk_length)[j]``); ``edges`` is
        ``[len(start), walk_length]`` edge offsets within each relation's CSR.

    Example:

    .. code-block:: python

        metapath = [
            ("author", "writes", "paper"),
            ("paper", "published_in", "venue"),
            ("venue", "publishes", "paper"),
            ("paper", "written_by", "author"),
        ]
        csr = build_metapath_csr(edge_index_dict, metapath)
        nodes, _ = metapath_random_walk(csr, mx.arange(10), walk_length=8)
    """
    metapath = csr.metapath
    m = len(metapath)
    if walk_length < 1:
        raise ValueError("walk_length must be >= 1")
    if walk_length > m and metapath[-1][2] != metapath[0][0]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"walk_length ({walk_length}) is longer than the metapath ({m}), "
            "so the metapath must be cyclic: it ends at "
            f"'{metapath[-1][2]}' but starts at '{metapath[0][0]}'"
        )

    start = mx.array(start) if not isinstance(start, mx.array) else start
    start = start.astype(mx.int64).reshape(-1)
    if rand is None:
        rand = mx.random.uniform(shape=(start.shape[0], walk_length))
    rand = rand.astype(mx.float32)

    step_rel = mx.array(
        np.array([csr.rel_ids[l % m] for l in range(walk_length)], dtype=np.int64)
    )
    return _metapath_random_walk(
        csr.rowptr,
        csr.col,
        csr.rowptr_offset,
        csr.col_offset,
        step_rel,
        start,
        rand,
        walk_length,
        stream=stream,
    )

def metapath_node_types(metapath: Sequence[EdgeType], walk_length: int) -> List[str]:
    """Node type of each of the ``walk_length + 1`` positions of a walk."""
    m = len(metapath)
    return [metapath[0][0]] + [metapath[l % m][2] for l in range(walk_length)]

def spmm_coo(
    row: mx.array,
    col: mx.array,
    x: mx.array,
    values: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    num_rows: Optional[int] = None,
    reduce: SpMMReduce = "sum",
    *,
    stream=None,
) -> mx.array:
    """SpMM with ``A`` given as a COO edge list (any edge order).

    ``out[r] = reduce_{e : row[e] == r} values[e] * x[col[e]]``

    GPU kernel: one thread per (edge, feature) with atomic adds (``max``/``min``
    use integer atomics on an order-preserving encoding of the floats).

    Args:
        row: ``[num_edges]`` destination node of each edge.
        col: ``[num_edges]`` source node of each edge.
        x: ``[num_nodes, features]`` node features.
        values: optional ``[num_edges]`` edge weights.
        num_rows: number of output rows. Defaults to ``x.shape[0]``.
        reduce: how the messages ``values[e] * x[col[e]]`` arriving at a row
            are combined, per feature: ``"sum"`` (or ``"add"``), ``"mean"``,
            ``"max"`` or ``"min"``. Rows without edges give ``0`` for every
            reduction. For ``"max"``/``"min"``, the gradient goes to every edge
            whose message equals the output (ties included), as in MLX's
            ``scatter`` max/min; ``mx.jvp`` is not supported for them.

    Returns:
        ``[num_rows, features]`` array with the dtype of ``x``.
    """
    reduce = _check_reduce(reduce)
    n = x.shape[0] if num_rows is None else num_rows
    out = _spmm_coo(row, col, x, n, values, reduce=_kernel_reduce(reduce), stream=stream)
    if reduce == "mean":
        deg = mx.zeros((n,), dtype=mx.int32).at[row].add(1).astype(mx.float32)
        out = out / mx.maximum(deg, 1.0)[:, None]
    return out.astype(x.dtype)

def spmm_csr(
    rowptr: mx.array,
    col: mx.array,
    x: mx.array,
    values: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    reduce: SpMMReduce = "sum",
    *,
    long_rows: Optional[LongRows] = None,
    transpose: Optional[CSRTranspose] = None,
    stream=None,
) -> mx.array:
    """SpMM with ``A`` given in CSR format (see :func:`coo_to_csr`).

    GPU kernel: one thread per (row, feature), no atomics, deterministic.

    Args:
        rowptr: ``[num_rows + 1]`` row pointer.
        col: ``[num_edges]`` source node of each edge, in CSR order.
        x: ``[num_nodes, features]`` node features.
        values: optional ``[num_edges]`` edge weights, in CSR order.
        reduce: how the messages ``values[e] * x[col[e]]`` arriving at a row
            are combined, per feature: ``"sum"`` (or ``"add"``), ``"mean"``,
            ``"max"`` or ``"min"``. Rows without edges give ``0`` for every
            reduction. For ``"max"``/``"min"``, the gradient goes to every edge
            whose message equals the output (ties included), as in MLX's
            ``scatter`` max/min; ``mx.jvp`` is not supported for them.
        long_rows: optional :class:`LongRows` (``CSR.long_rows`` from
            :func:`coo_to_csr`). Strongly recommended for graphs with hub
            nodes: without it a single thread loops over each hub's edges.
        transpose: optional :class:`CSRTranspose` (``CSR.transpose``). With
            it, the gradient w.r.t. ``x`` uses the CSR kernel on the
            transpose (deterministic); without it, the COO kernel.

    Returns:
        ``[rowptr.size - 1, features]`` array with the dtype of ``x``.
    """
    reduce = _check_reduce(reduce)
    kwargs = {}
    if long_rows is not None:
        kwargs.update(
            long_rows=long_rows.rows,
            chunk_ptr=long_rows.chunk_ptr,
            chunk_start=long_rows.chunk_start,
            chunk_end=long_rows.chunk_end,
            long_row_threshold=long_rows.threshold,
        )
    if transpose is not None:
        kwargs.update(t_rowptr=transpose.rowptr, t_col=transpose.col, t_perm=transpose.perm)
        lt = transpose.long_rows
        if lt is not None:
            kwargs.update(
                t_long_rows=lt.rows,
                t_chunk_ptr=lt.chunk_ptr,
                t_chunk_start=lt.chunk_start,
                t_chunk_end=lt.chunk_end,
                t_long_row_threshold=lt.threshold,
            )
    out = _spmm_csr(
        rowptr, col, x, values, reduce=_kernel_reduce(reduce), stream=stream, **kwargs
    )
    if reduce == "mean":
        deg = (rowptr[1:] - rowptr[:-1]).astype(mx.float32)
        out = out / mx.maximum(deg, 1.0)[:, None]
    return out.astype(x.dtype)

def coo_to_csr(
    row: mx.array,
    col: mx.array,
    num_rows: int,
    values: Optional[mx.array] = None,
    long_row_threshold: Optional[int] = 256,
    chunk_size: int = 2048,
    transpose: bool = True,
    num_cols: Optional[int] = None,
) -> CSR:
    """Converts a COO edge list into CSR (sorted by ``row``).

    This needs a sort, so compute it once per graph and reuse it.

    Args:
        long_row_threshold: rows with more edges than this get the
            load-balanced long-row path in :func:`spmm_csr` (see
            :class:`LongRows`). ``None`` disables it and keeps the conversion
            fully lazy (no host read-back), e.g. inside ``mx.compile``.
        chunk_size: maximum number of edges per long-row chunk.
        transpose: also build the transposed CSR (one more sort, ~3 extra
            index arrays) so the backward pass of :func:`spmm_csr` uses the
            CSR kernel: deterministic and atomic-free. Set ``False`` to save
            the memory when you only need the forward pass.
        num_cols: number of columns (source nodes), i.e. ``x.shape[0]`` in
            :func:`spmm_csr`. Defaults to ``num_rows`` (square adjacency).
    """
    row = row.astype(mx.int64)
    perm = mx.argsort(row)
    # int32 counts: MLX's GPU scatter does not support int64 inputs/updates.
    counts = mx.zeros((num_rows,), dtype=mx.int32).at[row].add(1)
    rowptr = mx.concatenate(
        [mx.zeros((1,), dtype=mx.int64), mx.cumsum(counts.astype(mx.int64))]
    )
    long_rows = (
        None
        if long_row_threshold is None
        else build_long_rows(rowptr, long_row_threshold, chunk_size)
    )
    col_csr = col.astype(mx.int64)[perm]

    csr_t = None
    if transpose:
        n_cols = num_rows if num_cols is None else num_cols
        perm_t = mx.argsort(col_csr)  # CSR edge index of each transposed edge
        counts_t = mx.zeros((n_cols,), dtype=mx.int32).at[col_csr].add(1)
        rowptr_t = mx.concatenate(
            [mx.zeros((1,), dtype=mx.int64), mx.cumsum(counts_t.astype(mx.int64))]
        )
        csr_t = CSRTranspose(
            rowptr=rowptr_t,
            col=row[perm][perm_t],
            perm=perm_t.astype(mx.int64),
            long_rows=(
                None
                if long_row_threshold is None
                else build_long_rows(rowptr_t, long_row_threshold, chunk_size)
            ),
        )

    return CSR(
        rowptr=rowptr,
        col=col_csr,
        values=None if values is None else values[perm],
        perm=perm,
        long_rows=long_rows,
        transpose=csr_t,
    )

def edge_scores(
    row: mx.array,
    col: mx.array,
    a: mx.array,
    b: mx.array,
    scale: float = 1.0,
    *,
    stream=None,
) -> mx.array:
    """Multi-head dot product per edge, the attention scores of graph
    transformers (e.g. ``TransformerConv``).

    ``out[e, h] = scale * <a[row[e], h], b[col[e], h]>``

    Equivalent to ``scale * (a[row] * b[col]).sum(-1)`` without materialising
    the two ``[num_edges, heads, channels]`` gathers. Differentiable w.r.t.
    ``a`` and ``b``: both gradients are computed with the SpMM kernels.

    GPU kernel: one SIMD group per (edge, head), all heads in one launch.

    Args:
        row: ``[num_edges]`` index into ``a`` (e.g. the destination node,
            whose queries are in ``a``).
        col: ``[num_edges]`` index into ``b`` (e.g. the source node, whose
            keys are in ``b``).
        a: ``[num_a, heads, channels]``, or ``[num_a, channels]`` for one head.
        b: ``[num_b, heads, channels]``, or ``[num_b, channels]`` for one head.
            ``num_a`` and ``num_b`` may differ (bipartite graphs).
        scale: factor applied to every score, e.g. ``1 / sqrt(channels)``.

    Returns:
        ``[num_edges, heads]`` (``[num_edges]`` for 2-D inputs), with the
        dtype of ``a``.
    """
    if a.ndim != b.ndim or a.ndim not in (2, 3):
        raise ValueError(
            "a and b must both be [num_nodes, heads, channels] or both "
            f"[num_nodes, channels], got shapes {a.shape} and {b.shape}."
        )
    single_head = a.ndim == 2
    if single_head:
        a, b = a[:, None, :], b[:, None, :]
    out = _edge_scores(row, col, a, b, scale=float(scale), stream=stream)
    if single_head:
        out = out[:, 0]
    return out.astype(a.dtype)

items.text:
build_long_rows(
    rowptr: array, threshold: int = 256, chunk_size: int = 2048
) -> Optional[LongRows]

Finds rows with more than threshold edges and splits them into chunks of at most chunk_size edges. Returns None if there are none.

Runs once per graph (it reads rowptr back to the host).

Source code in mlx_cluster/sparse.py 
def build_long_rows(
    rowptr: mx.array, threshold: int = 256, chunk_size: int = 2048
) -> Optional[LongRows]:
    """Finds rows with more than ``threshold`` edges and splits them into
    chunks of at most ``chunk_size`` edges. Returns ``None`` if there are none.

    Runs once per graph (it reads ``rowptr`` back to the host).
    """
    if threshold < 0 or chunk_size < 1:
        raise ValueError("threshold must be >= 0 and chunk_size >= 1")
    rp = np.array(rowptr, dtype=np.int64)
    deg = np.diff(rp)
    rows = np.nonzero(deg > threshold)[0]
    if rows.size == 0:
        return None
    n_chunks = (deg[rows] + chunk_size - 1) // chunk_size
    chunk_ptr = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(n_chunks)]).astype(np.int64)
    owner = np.repeat(rows, n_chunks)  # long row of each chunk
    local = np.arange(chunk_ptr[-1]) - np.repeat(chunk_ptr[:-1], n_chunks)
    start = rp[owner] + local * chunk_size
    end = np.minimum(start + chunk_size, rp[owner + 1])
    return LongRows(
        rows=mx.array(rows.astype(np.int64)),
        chunk_ptr=mx.array(chunk_ptr),
        chunk_start=mx.array(start.astype(np.int64)),
        chunk_end=mx.array(end.astype(np.int64)),
        threshold=int(threshold),
    )

Load-balancing metadata for CSR rows with many edges.

Rows with more than threshold edges are not handled by the regular one-thread-per-(row, feature) CSR kernel, where a single thread would loop over every edge of a hub node. items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Python 3.10 or later
  • macOS on Apple Silicon for the Metal kernels (a CPU-only build also works on Linux)
  • MLX 0.32 or later

items.title: From PyPI
items.text: pip install mlx-cluster

items.title: From source
items.text:
Building the Metal kernels needs Xcode (or its command line tools).

git clone https://github.com/mlx-graphs/mlx_cluster.git
cd mlx_cluster
pip install -e .

items.title: Check the installation
items.text:
from importlib.metadata import version

import mlx_cluster

print(version("mlx_cluster"))

If this prints a version number, mlx-cluster is installed and importable.

items.title: ImportError: No module named 'mlx'
items.text:
Install MLX first:

pip install mlx

items.title: Slow kernels
items.text: The GPU kernels need Apple Silicon. Check that MLX uses the GPU with mlx.core.default_device().

items.title: Quickstart
items.text: This guide will help you get started with mlx-cluster's graph algorithms in just a few minutes.

items.title: Random Walks
items.text:
Here's a simple example of performing random walks on a graph:

import mlx.core as mx
import mlx_cluster
import numpy as np
from mlx_graphs.datasets import PlanetoidDataset
from mlx_graphs.utils.sorting import sort_edge_index

# Load Cora dataset
cora = PlanetoidDataset(name="cora")
edge_index = cora.graphs[0].edge_index.astype(mx.int64)

# Convert to CSR format
sorted_edge_index = sort_edge_index(edge_index=edge_index)
row = sorted_edge_index[0][0]
col = sorted_edge_index[0][1]
_, counts = np.unique(np.array(row, copy=False), return_counts=True)
row_ptr = mx.concatenate([mx.array([0]), mx.array(counts.cumsum())])

# Set up random walk parameters
num_starts = 100
walk_length = 10
start_nodes = mx.array(np.random.randint(0, cora.graphs[0].num_nodes, num_starts))
rand_values = mx.random.uniform(shape=[num_starts, walk_length])
mx.eval(row_ptr, start_nodes, rand_values, col) #We need to call eval first since mlx uses lazy evaluation and the data won't be available
# Perform random walk
node_sequences, edge_sequences = mlx_cluster.random_walk(
    row_ptr, col, start_nodes, rand_values, walk_length
)

print(f"Generated {num_starts} walks of length {walk_length + 1}")
print(f"Node sequences shape: {node_sequences.shape}")

items.title: Biased Random Walks (Node2Vec style)
items.text:
For biased random walks with return parameter p and in-out parameter q:

# Biased random walk (Node2Vec style)
node_sequences, edge_sequences = mlx_cluster.rejection_sampling(
    row_ptr, col, start_nodes, walk_length, 
    p=1.0,  # Return parameter
    q=3.0   # In-out parameter
)

print(f"Generated biased walks with p={1.0}, q={3.0}")

items.title: Neighbor Sampling
items.text:
For GraphSAGE-style neighbor sampling:

# Convert to CSC format for neighbor sampling
def create_csc_from_edge_index(edge_index, num_nodes):
    sources = edge_index[0].tolist()
    targets = edge_index[1].tolist()

    edges = list(zip(sources, targets))
    edges.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])  # Sort by target

    sorted_sources = [e[0] for e in edges]
    sorted_targets = [e[1] for e in edges]

    colptr = np.zeros(num_nodes + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    for target in sorted_targets:
        colptr[target + 1] += 1

    for i in range(1, num_nodes + 1):
        colptr[i] += colptr[i - 1]

    return mx.array(colptr), mx.array(sorted_sources, dtype=mx.int64)

# Create CSC format
colptr, row = create_csc_from_edge_index(edge_index, cora.graphs[0].num_nodes)

# Sample neighbors
input_nodes = mx.array([0, 1, 2], dtype=mx.int64)
num_neighbors = [10, 5]  # 10 neighbors in first hop, 5 in second

samples, rows, cols, edges = mlx_cluster.neighbor_sample(
    colptr, row, input_nodes, num_neighbors,
    replace=True, directed=True
)

print(f"Sampled {len(samples)} nodes and {len(edges)} edges")

items.title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication
items.text:
Aggregate neighbour features without building a per-edge message array:

import mlx.core as mx
from mlx_cluster import coo_to_csr, spmm_coo, spmm_csr

src, dst = edge_index[0], edge_index[1]          # mlx-graphs convention
x = mx.random.normal((num_nodes, 64))

# sum / mean / max / min of incoming neighbour features
out = spmm_coo(dst, src, x, num_rows=num_nodes, reduce="mean")

# CSR: build once per graph, faster on medium/large graphs
csr = coo_to_csr(dst, src, num_nodes)
out = spmm_csr(csr.rowptr, csr.col, x, reduce="max",
               long_rows=csr.long_rows, transpose=csr.transpose)

See Sparse matrix multiplication for details.

items.title: Key Features
items.text:
• MLX Optimized: Built specifically for Apple's MLX framework
  • Fast Performance: Metal (GPU) kernels for random walks, SpMM and attention scores on Apple Silicon
  • Graph Algorithms: Random walks, biased random walks, and neighbor sampling
  • Fused message passing: SpMM (sum/mean/max/min) with gradients, on GPU
  • Flexible: Support for both directed and undirected graphs
  • Memory Efficient: Efficient CSR/CSC graph representations

items.title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication (SpMM)
items.text:
mlx-cluster provides fused sparse × dense matrix multiplication kernels for graph neural network message passing. They compute

\[ \text{out}[r, f] = \mathrm{reduce}_{\,e \,:\, \text{row}[e] = r} \; \text{values}[e] \cdot x[\text{col}[e], f] \]

where the sparse matrix A is the graph (one non-zero per edge) and x holds the node features. In message-passing terms, row is each edge's destination node, col its source node and values an optional edge weight.

items.title: Why use it
items.text:
The usual gather-scatter message passing first gathers x[col] into an array with one row per edge ([num_edges, features]) and then scatters it into the destination nodes. On large graphs that per-edge array dominates memory and time. The SpMM kernels read each neighbour's features and combine them directly into the output, so only node-sized arrays are ever allocated, in the forward and the backward pass.

Measured on an Apple M4 Pro (one training step = forward + backward, GCN layer, 1M edges, 256 features): about 4x faster and 4.6x less memory than gather-scatter (2.36 GB → 509 MB). The gain grows with num_edges × features; on very small graphs (e.g. Cora) it is about break-even.

items.title: Quick example
items.text:
import mlx.core as mx
from mlx_cluster import coo_to_csr, spmm_coo, spmm_csr

# edge_index = [src, dst], as in mlx-graphs
edge_index = mx.array([[0, 1, 2, 2], [1, 2, 0, 1]])
x = mx.random.normal((3, 16))
src, dst = edge_index[0], edge_index[1]

# COO: works directly on the edge list
out = spmm_coo(dst, src, x, reduce="sum")         # == scatter(x[src], dst, "add")

# CSR: sort once per graph, then reuse
csr = coo_to_csr(dst, src, num_rows=3)
out = spmm_csr(
    csr.rowptr, csr.col, x,
    reduce="max",
    long_rows=csr.long_rows,     # load balancing for high-degree nodes
    transpose=csr.transpose,     # fast, deterministic backward pass
)

# gradients work as usual
grad = mx.grad(lambda x: spmm_coo(dst, src, x, reduce="mean").sum())(x)

items.title: COO or CSR?
items.text: spmm_coo spmm_csr Input The edge list as-is, any order CSR from coo_to_csr (one sort per graph; cache it) GPU kernel One thread per (edge, feature); atomic adds One thread per (node, feature); no atomics Determinism Forward max/min are exact; sum/mean and all gradients w.r.t. x may differ in the last bits between runs Bit-identical results and gradients every run (with transpose) Best for Small graphs, or graphs that change every step Medium and large graphs (fastest in our benchmarks)

items.title: Reductions
items.text:
reduce selects how the messages arriving at a node are combined, per feature:

reduce Forward Gradient "sum" / "add" Sum of the messages A^T @ grad for x; one dot product per edge for values "mean" Sum divided by the number of incoming edges As sum, scaled by 1 / degree "max" Largest message Every edge whose message equals the output gets the full gradient (ties included) "min" Smallest message As max

Conventions, matching mlx-graphs' scatter:

  • Nodes without incoming edges get 0 for every reduction (not ±inf).
  • max/min are the true maximum/minimum, so an all-negative neighbourhood gives a negative result.
  • With max/min, an exact tie (e.g. a duplicated edge) gives the full gradient to every tied edge, exactly like MLX's scatter max/min gradient. The backward pass recomputes each message and compares it with the saved output, so no argmax array is stored.
  • All arithmetic is done in float32. Inputs of other dtypes are converted, and the result is returned in the dtype of x.

mx.grad / mx.vjp are supported for every reduction. mx.jvp is supported for sum and mean. Second-order gradients and mx.vmap are not supported.

items.title: High-degree nodes (load balancing)
items.text:
Real graphs often have a few nodes with a huge number of neighbours. A one-thread-per-node kernel would leave one thread looping over all of a hub's edges while the rest of the GPU sits idle. With long_rows (built by coo_to_csr), nodes with more than long_row_threshold edges (default 256) are cut into chunks of up to chunk_size edges (default 2048). Each chunk is reduced by its own GPU threadgroup, then the chunk results are combined in a fixed order. This keeps results deterministic, and for sums it is also more accurate than one long running sum.

On a 1M-edge power-law graph whose biggest node has 134k neighbours, this took the CSR forward pass from about 50 ms to about 1 ms.

Building long_rows reads rowptr back to the host once per graph, so it cannot run inside mx.compile. Pass long_row_threshold=None to skip it.

items.title: Fast backward pass (transpose)
items.text: The gradient of sum/mean with respect to x is A^T @ grad. coo_to_csr also builds the transposed CSR (csr.transpose, edges grouped by source node, with its own long_rows). When it is passed to spmm_csr, the backward pass runs on the CSR kernel too: no atomics, deterministic, and load-balanced for nodes with many outgoing edges. This holds for every reduction: for max/min each source node loops over its outgoing edges and adds the gradient of the edges that won (see Reductions). Without transpose (and with spmm_coo), the gradient w.r.t. x uses atomic adds instead, so it is correct but its last bits can vary between runs. coo_to_csr(..., transpose=False) saves the extra memory (about three index arrays) when only the forward pass is needed.

items.title: Attention scores (edge_scores)
items.text:
Graph attention layers (TransformerConv, graph transformers) weigh each edge by a score computed from both of its endpoints, typically the dot product of the destination's query and the source's key:

\[ \text{out}[e, h] = \text{scale} \cdot \big\langle a[\text{row}[e], h, :],\; b[\text{col}[e], h, :] \big\rangle \]

Gather-scatter computes this as (a[row] * b[col]).sum(-1), which first copies one row of a and one of b per edge (two [num_edges, heads, channels] arrays) to produce only [num_edges, heads] scores. edge_scores reads the two rows it needs for each edge and writes the score directly: one GPU SIMD group per (edge, head), all heads in one launch.

It is differentiable with respect to a and b, and the backward pass avoids the per-edge arrays too: both gradients are SpMMs,

\[ \frac{\partial L}{\partial a[:, h]} = \text{scale} \cdot \mathrm{spmm}(\text{row}, \text{col}, b[:, h], g[:, h]), \qquad \frac{\partial L}{\partial b[:, h]} = \text{scale} \cdot \mathrm{spmm}(\text{col}, \text{row}, a[:, h], g[:, h]) \]

where g is the incoming gradient of the scores.

Together with SpMM this gives a whole attention layer without per-edge feature arrays: scores, a softmax over each node's incoming edges (on [num_edges, heads] only), then a weighted sum with one SpMM per head.

import math

import mlx.core as mx
from mlx_cluster import edge_scores, spmm_coo

num_nodes, heads, channels = 1000, 4, 32
src = mx.random.randint(0, num_nodes, (20_000,))
dst = mx.random.randint(0, num_nodes, (20_000,))
q = mx.random.normal((num_nodes, heads, channels))  # queries
k = mx.random.normal((num_nodes, heads, channels))  # keys
v = mx.random.normal((num_nodes, heads, channels))  # values

# 1. one score per (edge, head): [num_edges, heads]
s = edge_scores(dst, src, q, k, scale=1 / math.sqrt(channels))

# 2. softmax over the incoming edges of each node
s_max = mx.zeros((num_nodes, heads)).at[dst].maximum(s)
e = mx.exp(s - mx.stop_gradient(s_max)[dst])
alpha = e / mx.zeros((num_nodes, heads)).at[dst].add(e)[dst]

# 3. weighted sum of the values, one SpMM per head
out = mx.stack(
    [spmm_coo(dst, src, v[:, h], alpha[:, h], num_rows=num_nodes)
     for h in range(heads)],
    axis=1,
)  # [num_nodes, heads, channels]

Conventions:

  • row indexes a and col indexes b, and the two may have different numbers of rows (bipartite graphs). With mlx-graphs' edge_index = [src, dst], queries are usually a (row = dst) and keys b (col = src).
  • 2-D inputs ([num_nodes, channels]) are treated as one head and give [num_edges] scores.
  • Arithmetic is done in float32; the result has the dtype of a.
  • mx.grad / mx.vjp and mx.compile are supported; mx.jvp, mx.vmap and second-order gradients are not.

sddmm computes the same single-head dot product but is not differentiable: it exists for the backward pass of SpMM. Use edge_scores in models.

Measured on an Apple M1 (8 GB), one TransformerConv layer from mlx-graphs (4 heads, 128 features, forward + backward): about 3x less memory at every graph size (2.74 GB → 0.84 GB on 500k edges) and about 2x faster on 500k edges, compared with gather-scatter.

items.title: Using it from mlx-graphs
items.text: mlx-graphs uses these kernels automatically in layers decorated with @fused_message_passing, for example GCNConv, SAGEConv, GINConv, GATConv, GATv2Conv and TransformerConv (which also computes its attention scores with edge_scores). It falls back to gather-scatter whenever the fused path does not apply, or with an mlx-cluster that does not have these functions. See the mlx-graphs documentation for details.

items.title: Limitations
items.text:
• SpMM messages must have the form values[e] * x[col[e]], with one scalar weight per edge (or per edge and head, one SpMM per head). Attention layers fit this form once their scores are computed (with edge_scores for dot-product attention), but messages that add a per-edge feature (e.g. TransformerConv with edge features, x[col[e]] + edge_attr[e]) still need gather-scatter.
  • softmax itself produces one value per edge, so it is computed outside the kernels, on [num_edges, heads] arrays.
  • Indices are processed as int64 and features as float32 inside the kernels.
